label: USE CASE 15
title: How Delivery Apps Predict Arrival Time

scenes.text: How do apps know, 32 minutes? You order biryani, and the app says, arriving in 32 minutes. [1] And somehow, it's usually right. [2] Let's break down how delivery apps predict arrival time.

The ETA is really three predictions added together. [1] How long the restaurant will take to cook. [2] How long until a delivery partner reaches the restaurant. [3] And how long the ride from the restaurant to you will take. [4] A model predicts each one, from past data, [5] and adds them up, 32 minutes.

So what does the model look at? [1] Distance and route, including one way streets. [2] Traffic, and time of day, like the evening rush. [3] Weather, because rain slows everything down. [4] And how busy the restaurant is, like a Friday night crowd.

Predicting a number, like minutes, is called regression. [1] It's supervised learning, where the label is the actual delivery time from past orders. [2] The model learns from millions of deliveries, [3] works out how each factor adds time, [4] and predicts the minutes for your new order.

data.definition: Supervised learning that predicts a number, like minutes, instead of a category.

scenes.text: And the ETA keeps updating. [1] When the restaurant marks the food ready, the model knows cooking is done. [2] GPS tracks the delivery partner, so travel time updates live. [3] And if there's a sudden traffic jam, the ETA adjusts, and you get a notification.
The same idea powers many apps. [1] Food delivery apps like Swiggy and Zomato. [2] Quick commerce apps, promising 10 minute groceries. [3] And courier and online shopping delivery estimates.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think the ETA is just distance divided by speed. [2] That's only a small part of it. Cooking time, partner availability, traffic and weather often matter more than the distance itself.

data.myth: The ETA is just distance divided by speed.
data.fact: Cooking time, partner availability, traffic and weather often matter more than distance.

Let's recap. [1] The ETA adds up cooking, pickup and travel time. [2] The model considers traffic, weather and restaurant load. [3] Predicting a number like this is called regression.
